- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.5) or shows strong reversal signals, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in the following days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If model forecast is >75% of historical 30-day average, consider mean reversion bias; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for next period unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 1,0,-1,0), model often misjudges turning points; use sentiment lag (e.g., 2–3 days) to smooth forecast transitions.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid forecasting >75% above recent 18-day high unless sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.8); otherwise, cap forecast at 18-day high + 2% max.
